A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, computational measurements and self-supervised finetuning outcomes in Section 5, Tables 1–6 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds diffusion-baseline comparisons, restoration examples and robustness results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 4 corrects the stated MOI finetuning objective, replacing the target A_r x_hat with x_hat. This changes the documented loss; an implementation change is not established. The main RAM architecture and supervised training objective are retained.

E1.justification: Appendix F extends evaluation to extreme-noise and low-retention inpainting scenarios on BSD68 samples. Super-resolution, denoising and inpainting already appeared in v1's training coverage; these are extensions within existing restoration tasks, with no new training dataset or imaging domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated DiffPIR and DDRM deblurring baselines, while Figure 11 introduces an evaluated SwinIR comparator for super-resolution. This substantially broadens empirical comparison, particularly by adding diffusion methods previously discussed without corresponding experimental results.

E3.justification: New DDRM comparisons use FFT-compatible blurring, circular input padding and non-overlapping 512×512 patches (Appendix E). Appendix F introduces controlled noise and masking sweeps and specifies the added super-resolution evaluation. Existing training budgets, splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained transfer and finetuning-size analyses, Appendix F adds Gaussian/Poisson noise-strength sweeps and comparisons across mask densities and masking patterns. It also examines an unfaithful repetitive texture in DDRM's deblurring output. These substantially expand direct investigation of robustness and failure modes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice; noise standard deviations describe corruption settings, not result uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–6 are retained, while v2 adds diffusion-baseline scores and reconstruction results in Figures 10–15. For example, Figure 11's first super-resolution example reports PSNR values of 27.2, 28.4 and 27.6 dB for DPIR, SwinIR and RAM. New DDRM results use adapted blur conditions rather than establishing a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the mathematical definition of the MOI loss and replaces consistency between measurements under different operators with consistency between reconstructed images. Other definitions and derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: lightweight reconstruction without unrolling, physics conditioning across imaging tasks, and adaptation through few-image self-supervised finetuning. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 qualifies deblurring comparisons by method class and attributes DDRM's advantages to near-invertible blur. Appendix F adds interpretations concerning preservation of low-frequency structure under extreme noise and masking-dependent failure around 20% pixel retention. The existing limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a RAM code-access link, discloses valid convolution padding, and specifies Cryo-EM input conditioning, crop normalization and zero nullspace loss. Appendix E documents DDRM padding and patch processing. The Cryo-EM disclosures do not establish changes to the previously reported experiment.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Kawar et al.'s DDRM and the Dhariwal–Nichol diffusion backbone. Previously cited DiffPIR and SwinIR become empirical comparators. The related-work narrative and central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized revisions to baseline, deblurring and Cryo-EM explanations, adds appendix cross-references and introduces Appendices E–F. The title, main section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reorganized with an explanatory legend, and Table 1 gains comparator rows, method-class grouping and bold performance indicators. Figure 4 replaces the displayed PDNet comparison with DDRM. Six additional figures substantially expand visual presentation of reconstruction and robustness evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more informative comparisons and failure-regime evidence, corrects the MOI expression and improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful but bounded gains: the new robustness sweeps use individual examples, and DDRM's different blur boundary treatment limits direct comparison. Together, the changes improve the paper's evidential clarity without resolving its broad claims comprehensively.
